/*
 * BUG-217 round 3 — WHO SAYS A QUEUED ROW WAS DELIVERED: the SERVER, by row id.
 *
 * Round 2's store (above) still left the delivery question to the tabs: a row
 * another tab marked `by` was never sent from here (and a killed tab never let
 * go — a follower stranded for minutes), and a row handed off before a reload
 * was judged by matching its TEXT against the transcript (an older message with
 * the same words made a new one vanish). Both were a tab reconstructing a fact
 * only the server has.
 *
 * Now every row gets a random `id` when it is created and keeps it for life.
 * Every automatic send of queued rows carries their ids; the server claims them
 * atomically and records them delivered at the handover (src/server/queue-
 * ledger.ts), so the same row can never reach the session twice, whichever tab
 * sends it, and a duplicate is answered `queue-duplicate` with each id's state.
 * A row stays in the queue — marked `sending` — until the server settles it, so
 * the store never declares a row finished before it is (no premature `done`).
 * A row whose fate this tab does not know (restored while `sending`, or another
 * tab marked it `sending`) is `remote: 'check'` and is asked of the server
 * (`reconcileQueue`); `in-flight` elsewhere is `remote: 'in-flight'` and asked
 * again until the server settles it. The store now carries only what the user
 * did to the dock (rows, edits, discards) — never who may send.
 */
const QUEUE_DONE_MAX = 200;       // tombstones kept per session — far more than any live queue
const QUEUE_DONE_TTL = 7 * 86_400_000; // an entry holding only tombstones is dropped after a week

/*
 * BUG-217 round 4: the id carries the row's birth time (`qt-<ms base36>-…`). The
 * server's ledger can forget an old row (it is capped per session), so it
 * answers `none` — never sent, go ahead — only for a row born after everything
 * it has forgotten; an older row comes back `uncertain` and asks the user.
 */
function newQueueId() {
  const born = Date.now().toString(36);
  try { return `qt-${born}-${crypto.randomUUID()}`; }
  catch { return `qt-${born}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 12)}${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 12)}`; }
}
/**
 * A row stored by a client that predates ids: deterministic, so two tabs
 * adopting the same legacy row name it alike (an id only — delivery is never
 * judged from it).
 */
function derivedQueueId(prefix, text, at) {
  let h = 5381;
  const s = `${at}\x00${text}`;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) h = ((h * 33) ^ s.charCodeAt(i)) >>> 0;
  return `${prefix}${Number(at || 0).toString(36)}-${h.toString(36)}`;
